description: Anger, forgiving someone who hurt you, guarding the tongue and gossip, humility, and keeping your intention sincere.

text.en: Anger is a wave you can learn to ride. Say that you seek refuge in Allah, sit down if you are standing, lie down if you are sitting, and make wudu with cool water. Stay quiet until it drops, because words said in anger are the ones people regret. The Prophet said the strong person is the one who controls himself in anger.

triggers: how to calm down when angry
doNotSay: If anger is with violence or fear of harming someone, move to safety and support; do not give a lecture.

text.en: Forgiving does not mean saying it did not hurt. It means choosing not to carry it. Start by asking Allah to ease your heart, wish the person guidance, and decide that you will not take revenge. You can forgive and still keep distance or set limits. Allah loves those who pardon, and the Prophet said forgiving raises a person in honour.

doNotSay: Never push someone to reconcile with an abuser; forgiving is not staying in danger.

text.en: To guard the tongue, pause before you speak and ask: is it true, is it needed, is it kind. The Prophet said whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day should speak good or stay silent. Backbiting is saying about someone what they would dislike, even if it is true. When a conversation turns that way, change the subject or leave it, and make dua for the person.

Humility is not thinking little of yourself; it is not thinking of yourself too much. Serve someone without being asked, accept advice without arguing, thank people who teach you, and say I do not know when you do not. The Prophet said Allah revealed that you should be humble so that none boasts over another.

Keeping your intention sincere is an ongoing job. Before an act of worship, take one breath and say silently that it is for Allah. If you notice you want to be seen, do not stop the good deed; just correct the intention and carry on. Do some good in secret that only Allah knows. The Prophet said deeds are by intentions.

triggers: how to keep my intention pure
how to be sincere to allah

text.en: To leave a sin, make it harder to reach and fill the gap. Remove what triggers it, change your company and your routine, and replace it with something good at the same time of day. When you slip, do not wait: make tawbah at once and do a good deed after it. Allah says good deeds wipe out bad ones, and the door of tawbah stays open.

triggers: i keep falling into the same sin
how to stop a bad habit
i keep doing the same sin
doNotSay: No shaming. If the matter is addiction, point to the support area for that topic.

text.en: Good company matters more than people admit. The Prophet compared a good companion to a perfume seller and a bad one to a blacksmith: one gives you something or a pleasant scent, the other may burn your clothes or leave a bad smell. Spend more time with people who remind you of Allah, and stay kind to the rest without following them.

With a difficult person at work or in the family, answer what is bad with what is better. Allah says that good and evil are not equal, and that then the one between whom and you was enmity may become like a close friend. Stay calm, keep your voice low, say what you need once and clearly, and keep your own conduct clean. You do not have to let anyone mistreat you; set limits politely, and speak to someone senior if needed.

triggers: a person at work hates me
i have a conflict at work
how to deal with rude people
doNotSay: If it is harassment or abuse, tell them to report it and seek help; do not tell them to just be patient.
